pairs.difference: A: the panel seams are thin, even lines and the sphere's contour stays continuous, with sand as a fine ripple texture. B: the seams swell into thick dark wedges at the lower panels, while the upper-left contour goes soft and nearly lost. Its sand is peppered with isolated hard dots and ringed blobs. Both are below the real subject edge density, so this is a weak call.
pairs.fix: Draw the seams between the ball's panels as thin lines of even width. Keep the ball's outer edge clean all the way round. Make the sand a soft continuous ripple with no scattered hard specks.

pairs.difference: A: the target rings and board edge are moderately weighted, the rim goes soft on its lit side, and the wall boards are faint. B: the target rings are near-equal heavy dark circles, the frame posts carry etched grain lines, and the teddy has dark closed contours at the feet and eyes. Line weight varies less across the card.
pairs.fix: Draw the target rings as clean colour changes, with no dark line between them. Remove the grain lines from the wooden frame. Let the teddy's edges soften into the fur.

pairs.difference: A: a heavy dark contour runs along the top and left of the unit, the grey trim strip is a thick double groove, and the wall stripes are very faint (background 0.005, below the real range). B: the unit edge is thinner and softens at upper left, the seam under the lid is a single fine line, and the wall stripe edges fall within the real density range. B's air streaks do have crisp line-like edges, so this is not clear-cut.
pairs.fix: Remove the dark line around the top of the unit and let the white casing meet the wall by tone alone. Make the trim seam one thin line. Give the wall stripes clearer, clean boundaries.

pairs.difference: A: the rims of the lid and banding are soft and rounded, the planks have sparse seams, and edges are selective and loosen away from the coins. B: every plank, metal band and rivet has a dark closed contour, the wood is filled with dense grain strokes, and sand and shell carry extra fine lines. Edge strength is the same on the chest's front face and at the coins, so there is little hierarchy.
pairs.fix: Keep the sharpest edges on the coins and gems. Replace dark lines around the metal bands with soft bevels. Reduce the wood to a few thin plank seams with no grain strokes.

pairs.difference: A: a dark, near-uniform contour wraps the crown and visor, and the wall and floor have dense swirling grain lines (background 0.05, above the real range). B: the contour is heavy at upper left but fades to lost edges along the right side of the crown, and the crown top is quieter. Its wood is also busy, though within range.
pairs.fix: Remove the dark line around the white crown and let it separate from the wall by value. Cut the wall and floor to plain plank seams with almost no grain swirls.

pairs.difference: A: the glazing bars are thin double lines, inner parts stay legible, and crowns are light background marks, though the interior is busy (0.238, just above the real range). B: the window openings read as heavy black closed rectangles, the booth base has a thick uniform contour, and the suitcases are large double-lined shapes with strong edges competing with the hero.
pairs.fix: Draw the window bars as slim red strips with thin clean edges, not black-edged boxes. Remove the dark line around the base. Make the background suitcases faint with soft edges.

pairs.difference: A: wall stripes and floor gaps are thin precise lines, the glove edges are crisp, and the cuffs have clean seams. B: the wall has thick dark double-line grooves that are stronger than the hero (background 0.04 against gloves 0.037), and the shelf edge is a heavy band. The gloves themselves are mushy with weak contours, so the edge hierarchy is inverted.
pairs.fix: Make the background stripes soft colour bands with no dark grooves, and make the table edge one thin line. Give the gloves the sharpest edges on the card, especially at the cuffs and thumb.

pairs.difference: A: edges are thin and vary along the fin rims and foot pockets, with fine crisp inner shapes and light rings behind. B: a heavy dark contour runs along the grey blade inserts and pocket openings. The wide orange rim reads as a broad doubled band with blurry ridges, and the fins have few internal edges (0.07 against 0.155).
pairs.fix: Make the grey blade panels meet the orange by a clean colour change with no dark line. Give the fin rim a thin crisp edge and add small precise moulded seams on the foot pockets.

pairs.difference: A: plank gaps and post edges are fairly thin and rope is small, though the water caustics make a busy cell pattern. B: the rope coils and ring trim have thick dark twisted contours, the life ring has heavy panel edges, and the water ripples are drawn as dark closed rings around the posts. The contours are heavy across the whole foreground.
pairs.fix: Show the rope twists with soft light and shade, not dark lines. Keep the band edges on the life ring thin. Paint the water ripples as pale soft shapes without drawn rings.

pairs.difference: A: the leaves are thick sculpted forms with edges that vary and lost inner edges, the trunk bands are soft, and the background rings are thin and faint. B: the leaf tips and notches are hard and pointed, and the trunk has dark etched bark strokes and heavy rings at the base. The spiral background has strong dark lines near the crown, plus horizontal streak texture at upper right.
pairs.fix: Keep the trunk smooth with a few soft bands and no bark scratches. Make the background rings faint and soft-edged, and remove the fine horizontal streaks. Soften the inner leaf edges.

pairs.difference: A: the locker edges are rounded and soft, the lid has no hard rim, and the shelf and vent lines are moderate. B: ruler-straight dark contours run along the lid and door, the door gap and frame are double lines, and the floor planks and baseboard are thick dark lines. The shoe laces are heavily inked, and line weight is uniformly strong across hero and floor.
pairs.fix: Round the locker's corners and let its edges turn softly with no dark line along the lid. Make the floor plank gaps thin and pale. Paint the laces as light shapes with no black contour.

pairs.difference: A: the slide has one clean rim line, and tiles and rail lines are thin and regular, though the water splash is busy. B: the slide is sparse inside but its lip carries thick doubled grooves. The pool edge is packed with dense small tile lines, the wave background is strong, and background density (0.065) is above the real range and higher than A's. The busiest edges sit away from the hero.
pairs.fix: Make the pool tiles large, with thin pale joints, and fade the wave background to soft colour shifts. Give the slide one clean rim edge with no doubled grooves.

pairs.difference: A: a thick dark inset groove rings the face panel, the central dial has several stacked rings, and the cable reads as a heavy double line. B: edges are sparse, with a clean disc rim, small button rims and a body edge that softens at the bottom, closer to thin controlled seams. Both measure in range, so this is a mild preference.
pairs.fix: Replace the thick groove around the player's face with one thin fine seam. Simplify the dial to a single raised rim. Draw the cable as a smooth tube with no dark edges.

pairs.difference: A: the envelope and photo edges are crisp, the inset landscape uses simple blocks, and folds are thin. B: the inset photo is packed with hatch-like micro strokes for trees, water and houses. The envelope has a thick swollen rim with a dark contour, and the stamp perforation and postmark are heavily inked. Edge density concentrates in the tiny picture, not the main form.
pairs.fix: Paint the small landscape in a few big simple colour shapes with no fine line detail. Make the envelope edge a thin clean paper edge, not a thick puffy rim, and lighten the postmark.

pairs.difference: A: the background is thin plank lines and pale stripes (background 0.012), and the glass rim and fruit edges are clean, with the hero clearly the sharpest area. B: dark diagonal streaks fill the wood background (0.037), the plate has several dark concentric contours, and droplets and blueberries have hard black rings (outline 0.061, above A's -0.056). The background competes with the fruit.
pairs.fix: Make the table a calm surface with a few thin plank gaps and no dark grain streaks. Draw the plate rim as one thin glassy highlight. Remove the dark rings around the water drops and berries.

pairs.difference: A: door panels are thin precise grooves, while the ivy is very dense (0.342, above the real range) and leaf shadows leave ghost edges on the door. B: the wreath flowers and ivy leaves have thick dark closed contours, the door boards and frame have etched lines, and wall cracks and paving joints are inked (background 0.12, above the real range). Both are overbusy, but B's lines look more drawn-on.
pairs.fix: Remove the dark outlines around the leaves and flowers and let them separate by colour and soft shade. Erase the wall cracks and reduce the paving joints to thin pale lines. Keep the door boards plain.

pattern: Generated cards give themselves away through line weight and where it sits. The contours are dark and nearly uniform around forms (lids, bases, window bars, rings). Grooves are thick or doubled where real cards use a single thin seam, or simply let two colours meet. Background and surface detail is over-inked: wood grain, water rings, tile joints, wall cracks and stripes. As a result the edge hierarchy goes flat or inverted, with little difference between focus and surroundings. Real cards keep edges selective, with thin seams, soft or lost contours on lit sides and calm backgrounds.
